title: Kestrel and the Cover
premise: Yara Okafor, a disgraced intelligence analyst fired from three agencies for refusing to falsify findings, receives an automated voiceprint unlock tied to her dead father's voice — opening a server in Lagos that documents 'the Cover,' a transnational program that launders sanctioned money through humanitarian aid. The server's dead-man switch gives her seventy-two hours before its contents scatter and the program's enforcers close in. Hunted by both the Cover's fixer and former colleagues ordered to bury her, Yara must decide whether to trade the archive to a corrupt senator for her brother's life or expose it and destroy her father's posthumous reputation, which she learns he built the Cover. She chooses truth: she broadcasts the archive, lets her father's name burn with it, and walks away cleared of nothing but certain of everything.
about_author: E. M. Ravensworth is the pen name of a former compliance investigator who spent a decade inside financial institutions before turning to fiction full-time. They write thrillers about people who discover that the systems they served were never designed to protect them.

chapters.title: Voiceprint
chapters.summary: Yara Okafor, three agencies fired and twelve years burned, gets a call from a number that plays back her dead father's voice asking for a passphrase she's never heard. POV: Yara. Emotional beat: grief curdling into suspicion — someone is using the dead to bait her.

chapters.title: The Server in Lagos
chapters.summary: Following the voiceprint handshake, Yara unlocks an encrypted server hosted in Lagos containing financial ledgers linking humanitarian aid flows to sanctioned regimes. POV: Yara. Emotional beat: analyst's thrill returning after years of numbness — she remembers who she used to be.

chapters.title: Seventy-Two Hours
chapters.summary: A countdown appears on the server: a dead-man switch will fragment the archive unless refreshed by someone with her father's biometric chain — meaning her. POV: Yara. Emotional beat: dread; the inheritance is a trap as much as a gift.

chapters.title: What the Agencies Knew
chapters.summary: Flashback chapter: Yara recalls the falsified report that got her fired from her second agency — the same ledger numbers now appearing on the Lagos server. POV: Yara (interleaved with her old supervisor Marcus Hale). Emotional beat: vindication and rage braided together.

chapters.title: The Fixer
chapters.summary: Introduce Adaeze Nwosu, the Cover's elegant enforcer, who arrives in Yara's city within hours of the unlock — proof of a leak inside Yara's circle. POV: Adaeze. Emotional beat: cold competence masking genuine respect for a worthy opponent.

chapters.title: Brother's Keeper
chapters.summary: Yara's estranged brother Tunde, a logistics manager in Rotterdam, is detained on fabricated customs charges — leverage. POV: Tunde. Emotional beat: fear and resentment; he blames their father's secrets for every fracture in the family.

chapters.title: Rules That Rewrite Themselves
chapters.summary: Yara approaches her first agency mentor, now a private consultant, who warns her off and then quietly slips her a name: Senator Calloway. POV: Yara. Emotional beat: betrayal of trust, followed by the first real lead.

chapters.title: Calloway's Offer
chapters.summary: Senator Calloway meets Yara privately: he'll free Tunde and shield her if she hands over the archive unbroken — he claims he's trying to contain the Cover, not protect it. POV: Yara. Emotional beat: temptation wearing the mask of justice.

chapters.title: Ghost in the Ledger
chapters.summary: Digging into the server's creation logs, Yara finds her father wasn't a whistleblower — he was an architect of the Cover who built the kill switch as insurance against his partners. POV: Yara. Emotional beat: the floor drops out; her moral anchor was the villain.

chapters.title: Safehouse Arithmetic
chapters.summary: Holed up with a skeptical freelance journalist, Priya Raman, Yara calculates what exposure costs: sources dead, aid programs collapsed, Tunde still jailed. POV: Priya. Emotional beat: the weight of truth as a weapon that wounds whoever holds it.

chapters.title: Adaeze's File
chapters.summary: Adaeze discovers her own employers plan to erase her once Yara is handled; she begins keeping her own insurance copy. POV: Adaeze. Emotional beat: loyalty to an institution curdling into self-preservation.

chapters.title: Rotterdam
chapters.summary: Yara flies to Rotterdam under a false passport to reach Tunde before transfer to a black-site detention pipeline. POV: Yara. Emotional beat: desperation sharpening into focus; family over ideology, for now.

chapters.title: The Handoff That Wasn't
chapters.summary: A staged exchange goes wrong — Calloway's men and the Cover's fixers converge, and Yara realizes the senator is a Cover partner playing both sides. POV: Yara. Emotional beat: betrayal confirmed; no deal was ever on the table.

chapters.title: Burned Bridge
chapters.summary: Marcus Hale, ordered to silence Yara, instead tips her to the extraction schedule — repaying the report she refused to falsify twelve years ago. POV: Marcus. Emotional beat: redemption bought at the price of his career and safety.

chapters.title: Tunde
chapters.summary: Yara and Priya spring Tunde from a holding facility using the Cover's own logistics codes from the ledger. POV: Tunde. Emotional beat: reconciliation forged in adrenaline; siblings finally fighting on the same side.

chapters.title: The Partner List
chapters.summary: Decrypted files reveal the Cover's partners include Calloway, two agency directors, and — most devastating — evidence her father funded it with her mother's estate. POV: Yara. Emotional beat: inheritance revealed as theft; the family fortune was always dirty.

chapters.title: Adaeze Defects
chapters.summary: Cornered by her own employers, Adaeze offers Yara the final authentication key in exchange for inclusion in the exposure — mutual hostage-taking becomes uneasy alliance. POV: Adaeze. Emotional beat: pride swallowed; survival requires trusting your hunter.

chapters.title: Seventy-Two Hours, Spent
chapters.summary: With the switch expiring at midnight, Yara must choose: sell the archive to Calloway for total immunity, or broadcast it and lose everything including her father's name. POV: Yara. Emotional beat: the quietest, heaviest moment in the book — a decision made alone at 3 a.m.

chapters.title: Broadcast
chapters.summary: Yara routes the archive through forty mirrors simultaneously; the Cover's takedown teams race servers they can't catch. Calloway's office burns on live feeds. POV: multiple, rapid cuts. Emotional beat: catharsis with teeth — victory that feels like detonation.

chapters.title: Reckoning
chapters.summary: Fallout: arrests, resignations, aid programs suspended while auditors move in; Tunde freed but the family name destroyed. Adaeze vanishes with her insurance copy. POV: Yara. Emotional beat: hollow triumph; justice outside the law leaves scars on the just.

chapters.title: What Her Father Left
chapters.summary: Among the decrypted files Yara finds one personal video: her father explaining why he built the kill switch — not remorse, but leverage — and one line meant for her. POV: Yara. Emotional beat: mourning someone she never actually knew.

chapters.title: Kestrel
chapters.summary: Months later, Yara declines every offer to return to the agencies and instead joins an independent oversight collective; a kestrel — her father's nickname for her — hovers on the wind outside her window. POV: Yara. Emotional beat: resolution without restoration; she chose truth and learned to live in the wind it made.
